summary_paragraph: A 78-year-old male with a history of severe aortic stenosis, diastolic heart failure, atrial fibrillation, and chronic bronchitis was admitted for worsening shortness of breath, orthopnea, and lower extremity edema. He had recently increased his furosemide dose at home without improvement. Evaluation confirmed acute on chronic diastolic heart failure exacerbation with bilateral pleural effusions and mild pulmonary congestion. He was treated with a furosemide drip, transitioned to oral torsemide, and showed significant improvement in symptoms and exam findings. A COPD exacerbation was treated with a short course of IV and oral steroids plus azithromycin. Digoxin was discontinued due to potential worsening of diastolic dysfunction, and warfarin was adjusted. Esophageal dysmotility was identified during evaluation of dysphagia, and iron supplementation was started for anemia. He was discharged home with home health services on optimized heart failure and COPD medications, with instructions to monitor weight, follow fluid and sodium restrictions, and attend cardiology follow-up for discussion of balloon valvuloplasty.
